variants:
- name: f_2asw
  description: Artificial seawater supplemented with half-strength Guillard f nutrients
    for marine diatom culture.
  modifications:
  - Supplement the artificial seawater base with half-strength Guillard f solution.
  - Use liquid or agar-solidified F/2ASW depending on maintenance, transformation,
    or selection protocol.
  - Reported diatom conditions include 20 deg C, continuous illumination at 30-75
    umol photons m-2 s-1, and aeration with ambient air or CO2-enriched air.
  purpose: Capture F/2 nutrient-supplemented artificial seawater as a recognizable
    variant of the 2ASW parent formulation.
  evidence:
  - reference: DOI:10.1104/pp.18.00453
    supports: SUPPORT
    explanation: Matsui et al. explicitly define F/2ASW as artificial seawater plus
      half-strength Guillard f solution for Phaeodactylum tricornutum UTEX 642 and
      Thalassiosira pseudonana CCMP1335 cultivation.
- name: modified_f_2asw_sodium_response
  description: Modified F/2 artificial seawater used to assay sodium and CO2 dependence
    in Chaetoceros gracilis UTEX LB2658.
  modifications:
  - Supplement F/2ASW with 10 nM sodium selenite and 0.1 mM sodium metasilicate.
  - Manipulate sodium by changing NaCl added to the basal artificial seawater.
  - Preacclimate cells to sodium concentrations before low-sodium transfer.
  purpose: Model experimental sodium-response medium variants without creating a duplicate
    artificial seawater parent record.
  evidence:
  - reference: DOI:10.1007/s10126-021-10037-4
    supports: SUPPORT
    explanation: Tsuji et al. report Chaetoceros gracilis UTEX LB2658 growth and carbon-concentrating-mechanism
      experiments in modified F/2ASW with defined sodium manipulations.
- name: 2asw_1_5_m_nacl
  description: Study-specific 2ASW reported by Liang et al. (2023). Only the explicitly
    stated NaCl concentration and algal cultivation context are resolved; full Table
    S2 formulation remains unverified.
  modifications:
  - The study reports 1.5 M NaCl in its 2ASW culture medium. This is a reported medium
    concentration, not a stock concentration or inferred amount to add.

    remain unspecified in the inspected paragraph. No salt-increase/decrease direction
    relative to this imported parent is asserted.

- name: bbm_estradiol_exposure_assay
  description: Study-specific BBM stock-culture and estradiol assay conditions. The
    study cites Stein 1973 for BBM; exact equivalence to this UTEX parent formulation
    is not established.
  modifications:
  - Adjust pH to 7.0 before use.
  - Aerate 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask cultures during the 11-day experiment.
  - Test separate 17-beta-estradiol treatments at 0.25, 0.75, 2.50, 5.0 and 15.0 ng/L,
    with a no-hormone control.
  - Maintain the pre-experiment Scenedesmus quadricauda stock culture in modified
    BBM containing 4.5 ppm NH4Cl; do not assert this as a universal final assay-medium
    dose.
  purpose: Experimental hormone-exposure growth assay using BBM as the base medium.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:35807621
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: 'The study was conducted using three types of media: Bold Basal Medium
      (BBM)'
    explanation: The paper explicitly used BBM as one of three media for the Scenedesmus
      quadricauda CPCC-158 growth experiment.
  - reference: doi:10.3390/plants11131669
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: 0.25, 0.75, 2.50, 5.0, and 15.0 ng/L
    explanation: 'variants[0].modifications[0:4]: the listed E2 levels are discrete
      active-estradiol concentrations, with a no-hormone control, not chemical-powder
      concentrations. Separately inspected Methods 2.1 excerpts: "NH4Cl was added
      to 4.5 ppm" (pre-experiment stock culture; unspecified ppm basis) and "250 mL
      Erlenmeyer flasks" (vessel capacity, not culture volume). Methods 2.2 states
      "adjusted to 7" for assay-medium pH. The study cites Stein 1973 for BBM; no
      exact equivalence to the UTEX parent or universal NH4Cl assay dose is asserted.
      Locator: Methods 2.1-2.3; reference 45.'

preparation_steps:
- step_number: 1
  action: MIX
  description: To approximately 900 mL dH2O, add the six Bristol mineral stocks and
    one drop each of EDTA, Iron, Boron, and Bold Trace stocks.
- step_number: 2
  action: MIX
  description: Bring the total volume to 1 L with dH2O.
- step_number: 3
  action: ALIQUOT
  description: Transfer the medium to a 2 L Erlenmeyer flask and cover.
- step_number: 4
  action: AUTOCLAVE
  description: Autoclave the covered Bold Basal Medium.

    is not established.

  - Test separate 17-beta-estradiol treatments at 0.25, 0.75, 2.50, 5.0 and 15.0 ng/L,
    with a no-hormone control.
  - Maintain the pre-experiment Scenedesmus quadricauda stock culture in modified
    BBM containing 4.5 ppm NH4Cl; do not assert this as a universal final assay-medium
    dose.

  action: MIX
  description: When cooled, add the sterile vitamin stocks.

  action: STORE
  description: Store at refrigerator temperature.

- name: n_replete_second_stage_tetraselmis_marina
  description: F/2 culture followed by nitrogen-replete second-stage cultivation for
    enhanced biomass and lipid productivity of Tetraselmis marina.
  modifications:
  - Grow cells in F/2 medium for seven days as the first stage.
  - Shift to a nitrogen-replete second stage with 4.41 mM NaNO3 for three days.
  purpose: Capture a study-specific F/2-derived nitrogen repletion variant used to
    increase Tetraselmis marina biomass and lipid productivity.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28456040
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: After second stage of cultivation of T. marina for further 3-days under
      N-replete condition (4.41mM NaNO3) increased biomass concentration of 1900mg/L
      and lipid content of 50% were observed
    explanation: Literature evidence describes a nitrogen-replete second-stage variant
      after initial F/2 cultivation.
  - reference: doi:10.1016/j.biortech.2017.04.008
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: N-replete condition (4.41mM NaNO3)
    explanation: 'Claims: variants[0].modifications[0:2], study-specific first-stage
      F/2 and second-stage nitrate concentration. Locator: abstract. Additional exact
      excerpt: "F/2-medium for seven days in the first stage". Retain 4.41 mM NaNO3
      without conversion; the abstract separately gives the three-day second stage.
      The phosphorus-repletion condition is a separate experiment. This does not define
      the complete medium or certify a strain; original PMID evidence is preserved.'
- name: f_2asw_diatom_culture
  description: F/2 artificial seawater culture conditions used for marine diatom maintenance
    and transformation studies.
  modifications:
  - Use artificial seawater supplemented with half-strength Guillard f solution.
  - Maintain cultures at 20 deg C under continuous illumination at 30-75 umol photons
    m-2 s-1.
  - Aerate cultures with ambient air or 1% CO2 depending on the experiment.
  purpose: Represent F/2ASW as a study-specific F/2 medium implementation for marine
    diatoms.
  evidence:
  - reference: DOI:10.1104/pp.18.00453
    supports: SUPPORT
    explanation: 'Matsui et al. define F/2ASW as artificial seawater plus half-strength
      Guillard f solution and report use with Phaeodactylum tricornutum UTEX 642 and
      Thalassiosira pseudonana CCMP1335. Claim: variants[1].modifications[0]. Locator:
      Materials and Methods / Cells and Culture Conditions. The excerpt supports this
      relative formulation strength only, not equivalence to the UTEX natural-seawater
      parent. Experimental nitrogen treatments are separate from maintenance medium.
      Source type: journal article; discovery: existing record reference; manually
      inspected full text.'
    snippet: artificial seawater supplemented with one-half-strength Guillard’s f
      solution
- name: modified_f_2asw_sodium_response
  description: Modified F/2 artificial seawater used for sodium and CO2 response experiments
    with Chaetoceros gracilis.
  modifications:
  - Use the modified F/2ASW formulation in Table S1, including 1 nM sodium selenite
    and 0.1 mM sodium metasilicate nonahydrate.
  - Adjust sodium concentration by altering NaCl addition to the basal medium.
  - Vary CO2 availability to distinguish sodium-dependent growth effects.
  purpose: Capture an experimental F/2ASW variant used to study carbon concentrating
    mechanism physiology.
  evidence:
  - reference: DOI:10.1007/s10126-021-10037-4
    supports: SUPPORT
    explanation: Tsuji et al. report Chaetoceros gracilis UTEX LB2658 growth experiments
      using a modified F/2ASW formulation.
  - reference: https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1007%2Fs10126-021-10037-4/MediaObjects/10126_2021_10037_MOESM1_ESM.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: '0.001'
    explanation: 'Claim: variants[2].modifications[0], Table S1 formulation only.

  description: Acetate-based water-soluble fertilizer medium developed from TAP for
    Chlorella sorokiniana cultivation.
  modifications:
  - Replace TAP trace and macroelements with water-soluble fertilizer.
  - Replace Tris in TAP medium with HAc-NaAc for pH balance.
  - Use the medium in fed-batch, semicontinuous, and outdoor cultures.
  purpose: Capture a TAP-derived lower-cost medium variant for Chlorella sorokiniana
    biomass production.
  evidence:

- step_number: 1
  action: MIX
  description: Bring to 1 L with filtered natural seawater.
- step_number: 2
  action: ADJUST_PH
  description: Adjust pH to 8.0 with 1 M NaOH or 1 M HCl before autoclaving.
- step_number: 3
  action: ADD_AGAR
  description: For an agar formulation, add 15 g/L Bacteriological Agar.
- step_number: 4
  action: AUTOCLAVE
  description: Autoclave at 15 psi for 15 minutes.
variants:
- name: f_2_silicate_supplement_1_06e_4_m
  relationship: SUPPLEMENTED_VARIANT
  description: Emami et al. (2015) f/2 supplemented with silicate for Isochrysis galbana
    CCAP 927/1; bounded supplement claim, not a fully resolved recipe.
  modifications:
  - The study reports f/2 supplemented with 1.06e-4 M silicate. Preserve this stated
    supplementation concentration without assigning an unreported silicate salt, hydrate,
    stock recipe or additional mass conversion.
  - Other nutrients, total silicate including the base, final-volume preparation and
    equivalence to local f/2 + Si records remain unresolved.
  evidence:
  - reference: doi:10.1038/srep10036
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: Isochrysis galbana was cultured using f/2 supplemented with 1.06 × 10−4
      M silicate
    explanation: 'Supports only variants[name=f_2_silicate_supplement_1_06e_4_m].modifications[0].

      Reported scientific name=Isochrysis galbana; strain=CCAP 927/1; canonical scientific
      name=Isochrysis galbana; NCBITaxon:37099; actual rank=species; taxonomy_match=exact_name_at_species_rank;
      lookup_url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Browser/wwwtax.cgi?id=37099;
      scope=silicate-supplemented f/2. Directly stated supplement value in the study
      medium, not a stock concentration or calculated total including background.
      No calculation. Local f/2 + Si owners specify sodium silicate nonahydrate and
      differently encoded stock amounts; the paper does not establish exact equivalence.'
- name: f_2_nitrate_supplement_29_4_mm
  relationship: SUPPLEMENTED_VARIANT
  description: Emami et al. (2015) nitrate-supplemented f/2 at pH 8 for reported Arthrospira
    platensis CCMP 1295; current NCBI synonym maps to Limnospira platensis.
  modifications:
  - The study reports f/2 supplemented with 29.4 mM NaNO3 and adjusted to pH 8. Retain
    the stated supplement concentration; do not infer whether it includes the base-medium
    nitrate or calculate a total nitrate concentration.
  - Remaining formulation details, chemical stock forms and equivalence to a specific
    canonical amount set are unresolved.
  evidence:
  - reference: doi:10.1038/srep10036
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: A. platensis was cultured using f/2 supplemented with 29.4 mM NaNO3 and
      adjusted to pH 8.
    explanation: 'Supports only variants[name=f_2_nitrate_supplement_29_4_mm].modifications[0].
      Locator: Methods / Microalgae and cyanobacteria strains and culture conditions.
      Reported scientific name=Arthrospira platensis; strain=CCMP 1295; canonical
      scientific name=Limnospira platensis; NCBITaxon:118562; actual rank=species;
      taxonomy_match=verified_synonym_at_species_rank; lookup_url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Browser/wwwtax.cgi?id=118562;
      scope=nitrate-supplemented f/2 at pH 8. Directly reported supplementation value
      and study pH, not a stock quantity or a universal optimum. No arithmetic; base-plus-supplement
      total remains unresolved.'
- name: f_2_penicillin_g_dihydrostreptomycin_supplement
  relationship: SUPPLEMENTED_VARIANT
  description: Emami et al. (2015) antibiotic-treated f/2 cultures of Dunaliella polymorpha
    CCAP 19/7A and CCAP 19/7C, separated from untreated controls and later bacterial
    marine-agar sampling.
  modifications:
  - 'Reported penicillin G treatment concentration: 200 micrograms per mL in the treated
    f/2 culture; no unreported salt form, stock strength or conversion is assigned.'
  - 'Reported dihydrostreptomycin sulphate treatment concentration: 50 micrograms
    per mL in the same treated culture; not streptomycin, not a stock concentration,
    and no hydrate assumption.'
  - The untreated comparator remains separate. Unspecified base formulation details
    and the later marine-agar bacterial assay must not be combined into this study
    variant.
  evidence:
  - reference: doi:10.1038/srep10036
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: 'treated with the antibiotics penicillin G and dihydrostreptomycin sulphate
      in a ratio of 200 μg mL−1: 50 μg mL−1.'
    explanation: 'Supports only variants[name=f_2_penicillin_g_dihydrostreptomycin_supplement].modifications[0:2].
      Locator: Methods / Bacterial interference experiment. Reported scientific name=Dunaliella
      polymorpha; strain=CCAP 19/7A; canonical scientific name=Dunaliella polymorpha;
      NCBITaxon:346903; actual rank=species; taxonomy_match=exact_name_at_species_rank;
      lookup_url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Browser/wwwtax.cgi?id=346903;
      scope=f/2 or double-strength f/2; general maintenance assignment unresolved.
      Reported scientific name=Dunaliella polymorpha; strain=CCAP 19/7C; canonical
      scientific name=Dunaliella polymorpha; NCBITaxon:346903; actual rank=species;
      taxonomy_match=exact_name_at_species_rank; lookup_url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Browser/wwwtax.cgi?id=346903;
      scope=f/2 or double-strength f/2; general maintenance assignment unresolved.
      These strain rows have a separate assay-specific assignment to f/2 in Methods
      / Bacterial interference experiment, not an unresolved maintenance-strength
      assignment. The two directly stated culture-treatment amounts share this exact
      excerpt; no arithmetic. Marine-agar sampling concerns co-occurring bacteria,
      not growth of Dunaliella on that agar.'
- name: f_2_2asw_vitamin_replacement_hiibel_2015
  relationship: SUBSTITUTED_COMPONENT_VARIANT
  description: Hiibel et al. (2015) f/2 maintenance medium with a reported 2ASW vitamin-solution
    replacement; composition and dose unresolved.
  modifications:
  - The vitamin solution described as coming from 2ASW replaces the original f/2 vitamin
    solution; the paper states it contains additional vitamin components.
  - Vitamin identities, stock composition, addition dose and resulting final concentrations
    are not quantified in the inspected methods. The cited Gomord 2010 reference is
    a plant glycosylation paper and cannot supply these missing details.
  - Other formulation details, physical-state equivalence, and exact correspondence
    to this imported stock encoding remain unresolved. This is not the silicate, nitrate,
    antibiotic or Quad formulation.
  purpose: Maintenance of the Table 1 brackish Nannochloropsis cohort, separate from
    wastewater screening.
  evidence:
  - reference: doi:10.3389/fenrg.2015.00020
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: the vitamin solution from the 2ASW medium (Gomord et al., 2010), which
      contained additional vitamin components, was used in place of that described
      for the original f/2 medium.
    explanation: 'Supports only the stated replacement in variants[name=f_2_2asw_vitamin_replacement_hiibel_2015].modifications[0].
      Locator: Materials and Methods / Strains and media. No numerical vitamin quantity,
      resolved complete formula or parent-medium growth is asserted; cohort names,
      strain designations, NCBI ranks and qualified taxonomy decisions are retained
      in this paper''s bibliography notes.'

- step_number: 1
  action: MIX
  description: Bring to 1 L with filtered natural seawater.

  action: ADJUST_PH
  description: Adjust pH to 8.0 with 1 M NaOH or 1 M HCl before autoclaving.
- step_number: 3
  action: ADD_AGAR
  description: For an agar formulation, add 15 g/L Bacteriological Agar.
- step_number: 4
  action: AUTOCLAVE
  description: Autoclave at 15 psi for 15 minutes.

variants:
- name: stl_medium_archaeoglobus_variant
  relationship: DERIVED_FROM
  description: STL (sulfate-thiosulfate-lactate) medium, a recognizable Archaeoglobus-type
    defined/complex medium used to grow A. fulgidus VC-16, distinct in formulation
    from the DSM 399 record.
  modifications:
  - 'Base built from a 10x salt solution (per L of 10x: NaCl 178 g, MgSO4 74 g, MgCl2.6H2O
    27.5 g, KCl 3.4 g, NH4Cl 2.5 g; Salt II CaCl2.2H2O 1.4 g; Salt III K2HPO4 1.37
    g) added at 100 ml/L.'
  - PIPES buffer 20 ml of 1 M per L; base medium adjusted to pH 6.7 (Hartzell 1999).
    Reed 2001 variant uses Tris+maleic acid 20 mM each, pH 6.1.
  - 'Carbon/electron donor: sodium lactate 7 ml of 30% (w/v) per L (Hartzell 1999);
    DL-sodium lactate ~22 mM (Reed 2001).'
  - Yeast extract 0.5 g/L (replaceable by Wolfe's vitamin mixture 10 ml/L for defined
    medium).
  - 1000x trace element stock (1 ml/L) incl. Na2EDTA.2H2O, Mn/Co/Zn/Ni/Cu/B/Al/Mo/W/Se/V
    salts; (NH4)2Fe(SO4)2 1 ml of 0.2% per L.
  - 'Reductant: Na2S 100 mM + Na2S2O3 200 mM stock added at 0.5% v/v after autoclaving
    (Hartzell); Na2S/Na2S2O3 ~1 mM each (Reed).'
  - Resazurin redox indicator; anaerobic, boiled and N2-sparged; good growth 75-82C
    (Hartzell), 83C in glass carboys (Reed).
  purpose: Capture the STL Archaeoglobus-type medium recipe used for A. fulgidus biofilm
    and enzyme studies as a variant of the DSM 399 parent rather than a duplicate
    medium.
  evidence:
  - reference: doi:10.1016/s0076-6879(99)10027-2
    supports: SUPPORT
    explanation: Hartzell et al. 1999 (Methods in Enzymology) prints the full STL
      medium recipe used to maintain A. fulgidus VC-16.
    snippet: A. fulgidus was grown in STL medium ... 10x salt solution 100 ml/L, PIPES
      buffer 20 ml of 1 M, trace element stock 1 ml of 1000x, yeast extract 0.5 g/L,
      sodium lactate 7 ml of 30% per L, pH 6.7; reducing agent Na2S 100 mM / Na2S2O3
      200 mM added 0.5% v/v; good growth at 75-82C.
  - reference: doi:10.1128/jb.183.24.7007-7016.2001
    supports: SUPPORT
    explanation: Reed et al. 2001 (J Bacteriol) reports a modified STL medium 3 for
      A. fulgidus, confirming the STL lineage and giving an alternate buffer/reductant
      variant.
    snippet: cells were grown anaerobically at 83C in glass carboys ... modified sulfate-thiosulfate-lactate
      (STL) medium 3 ... 20 mM Tris plus maleic acid, pH 6.1; DL-sodium lactate 22
      mM; yeast extract 0.5 g/L; Na2S and Na2S2O3 1 mM; resazurin.

preparation_steps:
- step_number: 1
  action: AUTOCLAVE
  description: Dissolve ingredients except bicarbonate, cysteine and sulfide. Sparge
    medium with 80% H2 and 20% CO2 gas mixture for 30 - 45 min to make it anoxic.
    Add and dissolve bicarbonate, adjust pH to 6.5 and dispense medium under 80% H2
    and 20% CO2 gas atmosphere into anoxic Hungate-type tubes or serum vials to 30%
    of their volume and autoclave. Add cysteine and sulfide from sterile anoxic stock
    solutions prepared under 100% N2 gas. Prior to use check pH of complete medium
    and adjust to 6.8 - 7.0, if necessary.
- step_number: 2
  action: MIX
  description: 'Note: After growth has started and the culture is becoming turbid
    add sterile 80% H2 and 20% CO2 gas mixture to 0.5 - 1 bar overpressure.'

- Microbial cultivation

preparation_steps:
- step_number: 1
  action: AUTOCLAVE
  description: Dissolve ingredients except bicarbonate, cysteine and sulfide. Sparge
    medium with 80% H2 and 20% CO2 gas mixture for 30 - 45 min to make it anoxic.
    Add and dissolve bicarbonate, adjust pH to 6.5 and dispense medium under 80% H2
    and 20% CO2 gas atmosphere into anoxic Hungate-type tubes or serum vials to 30%
    of their volume and autoclave. Add cysteine and sulfide from sterile anoxic stock
    solutions prepared under 100% N2 gas. Prior to use check pH of complete medium
    and adjust to 6.8 - 7.0, if necessary.
- step_number: 2
  action: MIX
  description: 'Note: After growth has started and the culture is becoming turbid
    add sterile 80% H2 and 20% CO2 gas mixture to 0.5 - 1 bar overpressure.'
applications:
- Microbial cultivation

step_number: 1 action: ADJUST_PH description: Dissolve ingredients except for sulfur, peptone, yeast extract, and sulfide, adjust the pH to 6.5 and sparge medium with 100% N2 gas for 30 - 45 min to make it anoxic. Distribute medium under the same gas atmosphere into anoxic Hungate-type tubes or serum vials that already contain the appropriate amount of sulfur. Sterilize the medium by autoclaving at 110°C for 20 min. After sterilization, add peptone and yeast extract from sterile stock solutions prepared under 100% N2 gas atmosphere and sulfide from a neutralized stock solution. - step_number: 2 action: ADJUST_PH description: First dissolve nitrilotriacetic acid and adjust pH to 6.5 with KOH, then add minerals. Adjust final to pH 7.0 with KOH. - step_number: 3 action: AUTOCLAVE description: The sulfide solution is prepared in a 250 ml screw-capped bottle with a butyl rubber septum and a magnetic stirrer. The solution is bubbled with nitrogen gas, closed and autoclaved for 15 min. at 121°C.     N2 gas phase'
  - 65-75C; pH 2-3 (acidified with H2SO4 or HCl)
  purpose: Aerobic sulfur-oxidation / comparative physiology cultivation of Sulfolobales
    (A. brierleyi, M. hakonensis, M. prunae, S. ohwakuensis, S. tokodaii).

  - 65-75C; pH 3.0
  purpose: Anaerobic growth testing of Sulfodiicoccus acidiphilus HS-1T.
  evidence:
  - reference: doi:10.1099/ijsem.0.001881
    supports: SUPPORT
    explanation: Sakai & Kurosawa 2017 Methods. Basal MBS recipe cited to another

    parent in atmosphere and nitrogen source; grouped here as a derived aerobic variant.
  modifications:
  - Low-sulfate Brock's salts base (MgSO4 reduced/replaced); NH4Cl instead of (NH4)2SO4
  - 10 g/L elemental sulfur; species-specific 0.2-1 g/L yeast extract (or sucrose
    + NZ-Amine)
  - 'AEROBIC: vented serum bottles with foam stoppers; NO Na2S reducing agent; NO
    N2 gas phase'
  - 65-75C; pH 2-3 (acidified with H2SO4 or HCl)
  purpose: Aerobic sulfur-oxidation / comparative physiology cultivation of Sulfolobales
    (A. brierleyi, M. hakonensis, M. prunae, S. ohwakuensis, S. tokodaii).
  evidence:
  - reference: doi:10.1128/mbio.01033-24
    supports: SUPPORT
    explanation: Willard et al. 2024 is the shared source for the aerobic DSM-88 variant
      across these strains.
    snippet: 'All Sulfolobaceae species were grown in a low-sulfate formulation of
      Brock’s Salts (DSM-88 medium) containing:'
  ingredient_changes:
  - action: REPLACE

      preferred_term: NH4Cl

        sulfate. Primary MgSO4.7H2O concentration equals0.25g/L already in this parent,

    stage: Willard2024 low-sulfate Brock's salts aerobic formulation
    evidence:

      explanation: Materials and Methods, low-sulfate Brock's salts and species-specific
        supplements; primary source inspected 2026-11-16. Primary formulation names
        NH4Cl; local anaerobic parent names ammonium sulfate. Primary MgSO4.7H2O concentration
        equals0.25g/L already in this parent, so no unsupported MgSO4 reduction/substitution
        event is emitted.
    notes: A scoped change event, not a fully expanded variant or a parent-formulation

      of (NH4)2SO4
- name: reduced_anaerobic_mbsy_h2_co2
  relationship: DERIVED_FROM
  description: Reduced anaerobic modified Brock's basal salt medium with yeast extract
    (MBSY) used by Sakai & Kurosawa 2017 for anaerobic growth tests of Sulfodiicoccus
    acidiphilus HS-1T. The genuinely anaerobic member of the DSM 2162 evidence set.

preparation_steps:
- step_number: 1
  action: AUTOCLAVE
  description: "Make up to 1 Litre Filtered natural seawater. Adjust pH to 7.6 – 7.8\
    \ with 1M NaOH or 1M\r\nHCl, prior to autoclaving. Autoclave at 15 psi for 15\
    \ minutes"
- step_number: 2
  action: MIX
  description: "Alternatively, use: Distilled water to 1 Litre and “Ultramarine Synthetica”\
    \ sea salts\r\n33.60g"
- step_number: 3
  action: MIX
  description: "Site selection for a good soil is very important and for most purposes\
    \ a soil from undisturbed\r\ndeciduous woodland is best. Sites to avoid are those\
    \ showing obvious signs of man's activity\r\nand particular care should be taken\
    \ to avoid areas where fertilizers, crop sprays or other toxic\r\nchemicals may\
    \ have been used."
- step_number: 4
  action: HEAT
  description: "A rich loam with good crumb structure should be sought. Stones, roots\
    \ and larger\r\ninvertebrates should be removed during an initial sieving through\
    \ a 1 cm mesh. The sieved\r\nsoil should be spread to air dry and handpicked for\
    \ smaller invertebrates and roots. It should\r\nbe turned periodically and picked\
    \ over again. When dry sieve through a finer mesh (2-4 mm)\r\nand store in an\
    \ airtight container away from light and heat."
- step_number: 5
  action: AUTOCLAVE
  description: "Soil is prepared as above. Air-dried soil and twice its volume of\
    \ supernatant distilled water\r\nare autoclaved together at 15 psi for 2 hours\
    \ and left to cool. The supernatant is then\r\ndecanted and then distributed to\
    \ containers in volumes suitable for making up batches of\r\nmedia. The aliquots\
    \ and their containers are autoclaved for an appropriate length of time\r\n(e.g.\
    \ 1 litre or less for 15 minutes) and are then kept in a cool place (e.g. a refrigerator)\
    \ until\r\nrequired."

preparation_steps:
- step_number: 1
  action: AUTOCLAVE
  description: "Make up to 1 Litre Filtered natural seawater. Adjust pH to 7.6 – 7.8\
    \ with 1M NaOH or 1M\r\nHCl, prior to autoclaving. Autoclave at 15 psi for 15\
    \ minutes"
- step_number: 2
  action: MIX
  description: "Alternatively, use: Distilled water to 1 Litre and “Ultramarine Synthetica”\
    \ sea salts\r\n33.60g"
- step_number: 3
  action: MIX
  description: "Site selection for a good soil is very important and for most purposes\
    \ a soil from undisturbed\r\ndeciduous woodland is best. Sites to avoid are those\
    \ showing obvious signs of man's activity\r\nand particular care should be taken\
    \ to avoid areas where fertilizers, crop sprays or other toxic\r\nchemicals may\
    \ have been used."
- step_number: 4
  action: HEAT
  description: "A rich loam with good crumb structure should be sought. Stones, roots\
    \ and larger\r\ninvertebrates should be removed during an initial sieving through\
    \ a 1 cm mesh. The sieved\r\nsoil should be spread to air dry and handpicked for\
    \ smaller invertebrates and roots. It should\r\nbe turned periodically and picked\
    \ over again. When dry sieve through a finer mesh (2-4 mm)\r\nand store in an\
    \ airtight container away from light and heat."
- step_number: 5
  action: AUTOCLAVE
  description: "Soil is prepared as above. Air-dried soil and twice its volume of\
    \ supernatant distilled water\r\nare autoclaved together at 15 psi for 2 hours\
    \ and left to cool. The supernatant is then\r\ndecanted and then distributed to\
    \ containers in volumes suitable for making up batches of\r\nmedia. The aliquots\
    \ and their containers are autoclaved for an appropriate length of time\r\n(e.g.\
    \ 1 litre or less for 15 minutes) and are then kept in a cool place (e.g. a refrigerator)\
    \ until\r\nrequired."

  description: MRS medium condition used to compare oxygen-level effects on bile salt
    hydrolase production and growth kinetics in Heyndrickxia coagulans ATCC 7050 and
    Lactiplantibacillus plantarum ATCC 10012.
  modifications:
  - Compare MRS medium with M17 medium for bile salt hydrolase production.
  - Evaluate oxygen concentration effects in MRS medium, including anaerobic and microaerophilic
    conditions.
  purpose: Capture strain-specific MRS growth and doubling-time evidence under the
    parent MRS medium record.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39353547
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: Cultivation of cultures in MRS and M17 media revealed that MRS medium
      enhanced BSH production by 235.98 % in H. coagulans ATCC 7050 and 147.37 % in
      L. plantarum ATCC 10012, compared to M 17 medium.
    explanation: The source directly compares growth-associated fermentation performance
      of the two named ATCC strains in MRS versus M17 and then reports oxygen-condition
      doubling times for the same strains.
- name: mrs_broth_bg24_ph_yeast_extract_optimization
  description: MRS broth growth optimization condition for Lactiplantibacillus plantarum
    BG24, comparing static and shaken cultures and an MRS broth condition adjusted
    to pH 6.5 with additional yeast extract.
  modifications:
  - Compare static culture with 100 rpm and 200 rpm shaking in MRS broth.
  - Compare original MRS broth at pH 5.7 with MRS broth at pH 6.5 enriched with 5
    g/L yeast extract.
  purpose: Capture strain-specific BG24 MRS broth growth optimization evidence under
    the shared MRS parent medium.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:38194015
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: The specific growth rate of L. plantarum BG24 was 0.416 h-1, the doubling
      time was 1.67 h, and the biomass productivity value was 0.14 gL-1 h-1 in the
      original MRS broth (pH 5.7) while higher values were found as 0.483 h-1, 1.43
      h and 0.17 gL-1 h-1, respectively, in MRS broth (pH 6.5) medium enriched with
      5 g/L yeast extract.
    explanation: The source directly reports quantitative growth kinetics for Lactiplantibacillus
      plantarum BG24 in original and modified MRS broth.

  description: MRS medium condition used to compare oxygen-level effects on bile salt
    hydrolase production and growth kinetics in Heyndrickxia coagulans ATCC 7050 and
    Lactiplantibacillus plantarum ATCC 10012.
  modifications:
  - Compare MRS medium with M17 medium for bile salt hydrolase production.
  - Evaluate oxygen concentration effects in MRS medium, including anaerobic and microaerophilic
    conditions.
  purpose: Capture strain-specific MRS growth and doubling-time evidence under the
    parent MRS medium record.

  - reference: PMID:39353547

    snippet: Cultivation of cultures in MRS and M17 media revealed that MRS medium
      enhanced BSH production by 235.98 % in H. coagulans ATCC 7050 and 147.37 % in
      L. plantarum ATCC 10012, compared to M 17 medium.
    explanation: The source directly compares growth-associated fermentation performance
      of the two named ATCC strains in MRS versus M17 and then reports oxygen-condition
      doubling times for the same strains.

  description: MRS broth growth optimization condition for Lactiplantibacillus plantarum
    BG24, comparing static and shaken cultures and an MRS broth condition adjusted
    to pH 6.5 with additional yeast extract.
  modifications:
  - Compare static culture with 100 rpm and 200 rpm shaking in MRS broth.
  - Compare original MRS broth at pH 5.7 with MRS broth at pH 6.5 enriched with 5
    g/L yeast extract.

    explanation: The source directly reports quantitative growth kinetics for Lactiplantibacillus
      plantarum BG24 in original and modified MRS broth.

    evidence:

- name: strict_anaerobic_halothermothrix_orenii_h168_growth
  description: DSMZ/KOMODO Halothermothrix orenii medium condition representing the
    original strain H168 thermohalophilic anaerobic growth evidence.
  modifications:
  - Maintain strict anaerobic cultivation conditions.
  - Use high-salt growth conditions centered on 100 g/L NaCl, matching the parent
    medium's approximately 101 g/L NaCl formulation.
  - Incubate at 60 C for optimal growth of strain H168.
  purpose: Capture strain-specific growth evidence for Halothermothrix orenii H168
    under the existing parent medium instead of creating a duplicate organism-named
    medium record.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:7520742
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: A long rod, present only in the 40- to 60-cm layer, was isolated at 60
      degrees C
    explanation: The source directly reports isolation of strain H168 at 60 C in a
      medium containing 100 g/L NaCl, which matches the high-salt Halothermothrix
      parent medium closely enough for a variant-level record.
  - reference: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/bioproject/16377
    supports: SUPPORT
    explanation: NCBI BioProject PRJNA16377 links Halothermothrix orenii H168 to complete
      genome assembly GCA_000020485.1 and BioSample SAMN00623047.

variants:
- name: Carini 2014 AMS1 phosphite utilization assay
  description: AMS1 alternate-phosphorus utilization experiment in Carini et al. 2014
    Figures 1-2, reconciled against this imported formulation. Composite differences;
    no single relationship enum selected. Parent preserved.
  modifications:
  - 'Relative to this imported parent: pyruvate 100 micromolar (parent 1 millimolar);
    glycine 5 micromolar (parent 50 micromolar); methionine 5 micromolar (parent DL-methionine
    50 micromolar). The paper does not resolve methionine stereochemistry.'
  - FeCl3 1 micromolar (parent 117 nanomolar). The AMS1 base source specifies FeCl3.6H2O,
    but its 117 nanomolar dose is overridden by the main assay.
  - 'Full vitamin mixture: B1 6 micromolar, B3 800 nanomolar, B5 425 nanomolar, B6
    500 nanomolar, B7 4 nanomolar, B9 4 nanomolar, B12 700 picomolar, myo-inositol
    6 micromolar, 4-aminobenzoate 60 nanomolar. Parent contains only biotin 4 nanomolar
    and thiamine 60 micromolar.'
  - AMS1 Table 1 base uses MgSO4.7H2O at 2.8 millimolar, not parent magnesium sulfate
    28 millimolar. Source hydrate forms also specify CaCl2.2H2O, MnCl2.4H2O, ZnSO4.7H2O,
    CoCl2.6H2O, Na2MoO4.2H2O and NiCl2.6H2O; corresponding parent forms are anhydrous
    or unspecified. Retain Table 1 molar doses for these unchanged-dose salts, without
    mass conversion.
  - 'No phosphate is added to the alternate-P assay base; omit the phosphate of original
    AMS1 Table 1. This is not a claim of zero residual phosphate: the Figure 2 inoculum
    was previously grown on phosphate.'
  - 'Added phosphite: 1.0 micromolar final, numerically equal to the parent''s 0.001
    millimolar. This supports the assay, not the complete parent recipe. Phosphite
    salt is printed as NaPHO3.5H2O; preserve this literal source formula without assigning
    a corrected stoichiometry or converting to mass.'
  - Base preparation follows Carini 2013 Media preparation (inorganic AMS1 autoclaved,
    then carbon-dioxide and air sparging; vitamins and organics added afterward),
    rather than the parent's generic dissolve-all/filter-all steps. Reported base
    pH 7.5-7.7 is not an optimum or a separate measurement of every 2014 assay.
  purpose: Test HTCC7211 utilization of phosphite as an alternate phosphorus source.
  evidence:
  - reference: doi:10.1038/ncomms5346
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: pyruvate (100 μM), glycine (5 μM), methionine (5 μM), FeCl 3 (1 μM)
    explanation: 'Assay-specific amendments, Methods p.5 Organism source/Cultivation
      details, Figures 1-2. Independently located exact excerpt (vitamins, Organism
      source): ''B 1 : 6 μM; B 3 : 800 nM; B 5 : 425 nM; B 6 : 500 nM; B 7 : 4 nM;
      B 9 : 4 nM; B 12 : 700 pM; Myo-inositol: 6 μM; 4-aminobenzoate: 60 nM''. Exact
      substrate excerpt (Cultivation details): ''1.0 μM phosphite (as NaPHO 3 ·5H
      2 O)''. Exact final-basis excerpt (Figure 2 caption): ''Each alternate phosphorus
      compound was supplied at a final concentration of 1.0 μM.''. Exact omission
      excerpt (Organism source): ''without added P i''. Exact inoculum excerpt (Figure
      2): ''Cell inoculum was previously grown on P i .''. These are separate contiguous
      excerpts, normalized for whitespace only; chemistry is not repaired. Conversion
      outside quotations: 1 millimolar = 1000 micromolar; 0.001 millimolar = 1 micromolar;
      0.05 millimolar = 50 micromolar; 0.06 millimolar = 60 micromolar; 0.000117 millimolar
      = 117 nanomolar. The 2014 microarray protocol''s 1 millimolar pyruvate/50 micromolar
      glycine/50 micromolar methionine is not this alternate-P assay. Phosphite salt
      is printed as NaPHO3.5H2O; preserve this literal source formula without assigning
      a corrected stoichiometry or converting to mass.'
  - reference: doi:10.1038/ismej.2012.122
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: MgSO 4 ·7H 2 O 2.8 mℳ
    explanation: 'Cited base source, Table 1 heading=''Compound Final concentration'';
      separate exact table rows: ''NaCl 481 mℳ''; ''MgCl 2 ·6H 2 O 27 mℳ''; ''CaCl
      2 ·2H 2 O 10 mℳ''; ''KCl 9 mℳ''; ''NaHCO 3 6 mℳ''; ''MgSO 4 ·7H 2 O 2.8 mℳ'';
      ''''; ''(NH 4 ) 2 SO 4 400 μℳ''; ''NaH 2 PO 4 (pH 7.5) 50 μℳ''; ''''; ''FeCl
      3 ·6H 2 O 117 nℳ''; ''MnCl 2 ·4H 2 O 9 nℳ''; ''ZnSO 4 ·7H 2 O 800 pM''; ''CoCl
      2 ·6H 2 O 500 pM''; ''Na 2 MoO 4 ·2H 2 O 300 pM''; ''Na 2 SeO 3 1 nℳ''; ''NiCl
      2 ·6H 2 O 1 nℳ''; ''''; ''B 1 6 μℳ''; ''B 3 800 nℳ''; ''B 5 425 nℳ''; ''B 6
      500 nℳ''; ''B 7 4 nℳ''; ''B 9 4 nℳ''; ''B 12 700 pM''; ''Myo-inositol 6 μℳ'';
      ''4-Aminobenzoic acid 60 nℳ''. Table uses the script-M molarity glyph; m-script-M
      is millimolar, not a mass unit. The main 2014 assay overrides phosphate, FeCl3
      and organic amendments; do not inherit the base phosphate or base Fe dose. Separate
      exact preparation passage (Media preparation): ''Media preparation Artificial
      seawater medium AMS1 ( Table 1 ) was derived from the artificial seawater medium
      AMP1 ( Moore et al. , 2007 ). Organic buffers (for example, HEPES and EDTA)
      were excluded to avoid potential toxic effects ( Zigler et al. , 1985 ) and
      the possibility that they might be used as substrates for growth ( Nörtemann,
      1992 ). After autoclaving, AMS1 was sparged with 0.1 μm-filtered CO 2 for 5
      h followed by sparging with air for 10 h to establish a bicarbonate-based buffer
      system ( Connon and Giovannoni, 2002 ). All vitamins and organics were added
      after autoclaving and sparging. The pH of the resulting AMS1 typically ranged
      from 7.5 to 7.7. ''. No parent amount or preparation step is changed or newly
      certified; this evidence is attached to the named study variant only.'

  modifications:
  - 'Relative to this imported parent: pyruvate 100 micromolar (parent 1 millimolar);
    glycine 5 micromolar (parent 50 micromolar); methionine 5 micromolar (parent DL-methionine
    50 micromolar). The paper does not resolve methionine stereochemistry.'
  - FeCl3 1 micromolar (parent 117 nanomolar). The AMS1 base source specifies FeCl3.6H2O,
    but its 117 nanomolar dose is overridden by the main assay.
  - 'Full vitamin mixture: B1 6 micromolar, B3 800 nanomolar, B5 425 nanomolar, B6
    500 nanomolar, B7 4 nanomolar, B9 4 nanomolar, B12 700 picomolar, myo-inositol
    6 micromolar, 4-aminobenzoate 60 nanomolar. Parent contains only biotin 4 nanomolar
    and thiamine 60 micromolar.'

    28 millimolar. Source hydrate forms also specify CaCl2.2H2O, MnCl2.4H2O, ZnSO4.7H2O,
    CoCl2.6H2O, Na2MoO4.2H2O and NiCl2.6H2O; corresponding parent forms are anhydrous

variants:
- name: Carini 2014 AMS1 glucose 6-phosphate utilization assay
  description: AMS1 alternate-phosphorus utilization experiment in Carini et al. 2014
    Figures 1-2, reconciled against this imported formulation. Composite differences;
    no single relationship enum selected. Parent preserved.
  modifications:
  - 'Relative to this imported parent: pyruvate 100 micromolar (parent 1 millimolar);
    glycine 5 micromolar (parent 50 micromolar); methionine 5 micromolar (parent DL-methionine
    50 micromolar). The paper does not resolve methionine stereochemistry.'
  - FeCl3 1 micromolar (parent 117 nanomolar). The AMS1 base source specifies FeCl3.6H2O,
    but its 117 nanomolar dose is overridden by the main assay.
  - 'Full vitamin mixture: B1 6 micromolar, B3 800 nanomolar, B5 425 nanomolar, B6
    500 nanomolar, B7 4 nanomolar, B9 4 nanomolar, B12 700 picomolar, myo-inositol
    6 micromolar, 4-aminobenzoate 60 nanomolar. Parent contains only biotin 4 nanomolar
    and thiamine 60 micromolar.'
  - AMS1 Table 1 base uses MgSO4.7H2O at 2.8 millimolar, not parent magnesium sulfate
    28 millimolar. Source hydrate forms also specify CaCl2.2H2O, MnCl2.4H2O, ZnSO4.7H2O,
    CoCl2.6H2O, Na2MoO4.2H2O and NiCl2.6H2O; corresponding parent forms are anhydrous
    or unspecified. Retain Table 1 molar doses for these unchanged-dose salts, without
    mass conversion.
  - 'No phosphate is added to the alternate-P assay base; omit the phosphate of original
    AMS1 Table 1. This is not a claim of zero residual phosphate: the Figure 2 inoculum
    was previously grown on phosphate.'
  - 'Added glucose 6-phosphate: 1.0 micromolar final, numerically equal to the parent''s
    0.001 millimolar. This supports the assay, not the complete parent recipe. The
    paper does not specify D/L stereochemistry for this phosphorus substrate; do not
    certify the parent''s stereoisomer. Figure 1''s axis says Glucose-5P; Methods,
    Results and Figure 2 identify glucose 6-phosphate. This variant follows those
    concordant textual identities and retains the figure-label conflict.'
  - Base preparation follows Carini 2013 Media preparation (inorganic AMS1 autoclaved,
    then carbon-dioxide and air sparging; vitamins and organics added afterward),
    rather than the parent's generic dissolve-all/filter-all steps. Reported base
    pH 7.5-7.7 is not an optimum or a separate measurement of every 2014 assay.
  purpose: Test HTCC7211 utilization of glucose 6-phosphate as an alternate phosphorus
    source.
  evidence:
  - reference: doi:10.1038/ncomms5346
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: pyruvate (100 μM), glycine (5 μM), methionine (5 μM), FeCl 3 (1 μM)
    explanation: 'Assay-specific amendments, Methods p.5 Organism source/Cultivation
      details, Figures 1-2. Independently located exact excerpt (vitamins, Organism
      source): ''B 1 : 6 μM; B 3 : 800 nM; B 5 : 425 nM; B 6 : 500 nM; B 7 : 4 nM;
      B 9 : 4 nM; B 12 : 700 pM; Myo-inositol: 6 μM; 4-aminobenzoate: 60 nM''. Exact
      substrate excerpt (Cultivation details): ''1.0 μM glucose 6-phosphate''. Exact
      final-basis excerpt (Figure 2 caption): ''Each alternate phosphorus compound
      was supplied at a final concentration of 1.0 μM.''. Exact omission excerpt (Organism
      source): ''without added P i''. Exact inoculum excerpt (Figure 2): ''Cell inoculum
      was previously grown on P i .''. These are separate contiguous excerpts, normalized
      for whitespace only; chemistry is not repaired. Conversion outside quotations:
      1 millimolar = 1000 micromolar; 0.001 millimolar = 1 micromolar; 0.05 millimolar
      = 50 micromolar; 0.06 millimolar = 60 micromolar; 0.000117 millimolar = 117
      nanomolar. The 2014 microarray protocol''s 1 millimolar pyruvate/50 micromolar
      glycine/50 micromolar methionine is not this alternate-P assay. The paper does
      not specify D/L stereochemistry for this phosphorus substrate; do not certify
      the parent''s stereoisomer. Figure 1''s axis says Glucose-5P; Methods, Results
      and Figure 2 identify glucose 6-phosphate. This variant follows those concordant
      textual identities and retains the figure-label conflict.'
  - reference: doi:10.1038/ismej.2012.122
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: MgSO 4 ·7H 2 O 2.8 mℳ
    explanation: 'Cited base source, Table 1 heading=''Compound Final concentration'';
      separate exact table rows: ''NaCl 481 mℳ''; ''MgCl 2 ·6H 2 O 27 mℳ''; ''CaCl
      2 ·2H 2 O 10 mℳ''; ''KCl 9 mℳ''; ''NaHCO 3 6 mℳ''; ''MgSO 4 ·7H 2 O 2.8 mℳ'';
      ''''; ''(NH 4 ) 2 SO 4 400 μℳ''; ''NaH 2 PO 4 (pH 7.5) 50 μℳ''; ''''; ''FeCl
      3 ·6H 2 O 117 nℳ''; ''MnCl 2 ·4H 2 O 9 nℳ''; ''ZnSO 4 ·7H 2 O 800 pM''; ''CoCl
      2 ·6H 2 O 500 pM''; ''Na 2 MoO 4 ·2H 2 O 300 pM''; ''Na 2 SeO 3 1 nℳ''; ''NiCl
      2 ·6H 2 O 1 nℳ''; ''''; ''B 1 6 μℳ''; ''B 3 800 nℳ''; ''B 5 425 nℳ''; ''B 6
      500 nℳ''; ''B 7 4 nℳ''; ''B 9 4 nℳ''; ''B 12 700 pM''; ''Myo-inositol 6 μℳ'';
      ''4-Aminobenzoic acid 60 nℳ''. Table uses the script-M molarity glyph; m-script-M
      is millimolar, not a mass unit. The main 2014 assay overrides phosphate, FeCl3
      and organic amendments; do not inherit the base phosphate or base Fe dose. Separate
      exact preparation passage (Media preparation): ''Media preparation Artificial
      seawater medium AMS1 ( Table 1 ) was derived from the artificial seawater medium
      AMP1 ( Moore et al. , 2007 ). Organic buffers (for example, HEPES and EDTA)
      were excluded to avoid potential toxic effects ( Zigler et al. , 1985 ) and
      the possibility that they might be used as substrates for growth ( Nörtemann,
      1992 ). After autoclaving, AMS1 was sparged with 0.1 μm-filtered CO 2 for 5
      h followed by sparging with air for 10 h to establish a bicarbonate-based buffer
      system ( Connon and Giovannoni, 2002 ). All vitamins and organics were added
      after autoclaving and sparging. The pH of the resulting AMS1 typically ranged
      from 7.5 to 7.7. ''. No parent amount or preparation step is changed or newly
      certified; this evidence is attached to the named study variant only.'

variants:
- name: Carini 2014 AMS1 ribose 5-phosphate utilization assay
  description: AMS1 alternate-phosphorus utilization experiment in Carini et al. 2014
    Figures 1-2, reconciled against this imported formulation. Composite differences;
    no single relationship enum selected. Parent preserved.
  modifications:
  - 'Relative to this imported parent: pyruvate 100 micromolar (parent 1 millimolar);
    glycine 5 micromolar (parent 50 micromolar); methionine 5 micromolar (parent DL-methionine
    50 micromolar). The paper does not resolve methionine stereochemistry.'
  - FeCl3 1 micromolar (parent 117 nanomolar). The AMS1 base source specifies FeCl3.6H2O,
    but its 117 nanomolar dose is overridden by the main assay.
  - 'Full vitamin mixture: B1 6 micromolar, B3 800 nanomolar, B5 425 nanomolar, B6
    500 nanomolar, B7 4 nanomolar, B9 4 nanomolar, B12 700 picomolar, myo-inositol
    6 micromolar, 4-aminobenzoate 60 nanomolar. Parent contains only biotin 4 nanomolar
    and thiamine 60 micromolar.'
  - AMS1 Table 1 base uses MgSO4.7H2O at 2.8 millimolar, not parent magnesium sulfate
    28 millimolar. Source hydrate forms also specify CaCl2.2H2O, MnCl2.4H2O, ZnSO4.7H2O,
    CoCl2.6H2O, Na2MoO4.2H2O and NiCl2.6H2O; corresponding parent forms are anhydrous
    or unspecified. Retain Table 1 molar doses for these unchanged-dose salts, without
    mass conversion.
  - 'No phosphate is added to the alternate-P assay base; omit the phosphate of original
    AMS1 Table 1. This is not a claim of zero residual phosphate: the Figure 2 inoculum
    was previously grown on phosphate.'
  - 'Added ribose 5-phosphate: 1.0 micromolar final, numerically equal to the parent''s
    0.001 millimolar. This supports the assay, not the complete parent recipe. The
    paper does not specify D/L stereochemistry for this phosphorus substrate; do not
    certify the parent''s stereoisomer.'
  - Base preparation follows Carini 2013 Media preparation (inorganic AMS1 autoclaved,
    then carbon-dioxide and air sparging; vitamins and organics added afterward),
    rather than the parent's generic dissolve-all/filter-all steps. Reported base
    pH 7.5-7.7 is not an optimum or a separate measurement of every 2014 assay.
  purpose: Test HTCC7211 utilization of ribose 5-phosphate as an alternate phosphorus
    source.
  evidence:
  - reference: doi:10.1038/ncomms5346
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: pyruvate (100 μM), glycine (5 μM), methionine (5 μM), FeCl 3 (1 μM)
    explanation: 'Assay-specific amendments, Methods p.5 Organism source/Cultivation
      details, Figures 1-2. Independently located exact excerpt (vitamins, Organism
      source): ''B 1 : 6 μM; B 3 : 800 nM; B 5 : 425 nM; B 6 : 500 nM; B 7 : 4 nM;
      B 9 : 4 nM; B 12 : 700 pM; Myo-inositol: 6 μM; 4-aminobenzoate: 60 nM''. Exact
      substrate excerpt (Cultivation details): ''1.0 μM ribose 5-phosphate''. Exact
      final-basis excerpt (Figure 2 caption): ''Each alternate phosphorus compound
      was supplied at a final concentration of 1.0 μM.''. Exact omission excerpt (Organism
      source): ''without added P i''. Exact inoculum excerpt (Figure 2): ''Cell inoculum
      was previously grown on P i .''. These are separate contiguous excerpts, normalized
      for whitespace only; chemistry is not repaired. Conversion outside quotations:
      1 millimolar = 1000 micromolar; 0.001 millimolar = 1 micromolar; 0.05 millimolar
      = 50 micromolar; 0.06 millimolar = 60 micromolar; 0.000117 millimolar = 117
      nanomolar. The 2014 microarray protocol''s 1 millimolar pyruvate/50 micromolar
      glycine/50 micromolar methionine is not this alternate-P assay. The paper does
      not specify D/L stereochemistry for this phosphorus substrate; do not certify
      the parent''s stereoisomer.'
  - reference: doi:10.1038/ismej.2012.122
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: MgSO 4 ·7H 2 O 2.8 mℳ
    explanation: 'Cited base source, Table 1 heading=''Compound Final concentration'';
      separate exact table rows: ''NaCl 481 mℳ''; ''MgCl 2 ·6H 2 O 27 mℳ''; ''CaCl
      2 ·2H 2 O 10 mℳ''; ''KCl 9 mℳ''; ''NaHCO 3 6 mℳ''; ''MgSO 4 ·7H 2 O 2.8 mℳ'';
      ''''; ''(NH 4 ) 2 SO 4 400 μℳ''; ''NaH 2 PO 4 (pH 7.5) 50 μℳ''; ''''; ''FeCl
      3 ·6H 2 O 117 nℳ''; ''MnCl 2 ·4H 2 O 9 nℳ''; ''ZnSO 4 ·7H 2 O 800 pM''; ''CoCl
      2 ·6H 2 O 500 pM''; ''Na 2 MoO 4 ·2H 2 O 300 pM''; ''Na 2 SeO 3 1 nℳ''; ''NiCl
      2 ·6H 2 O 1 nℳ''; ''''; ''B 1 6 μℳ''; ''B 3 800 nℳ''; ''B 5 425 nℳ''; ''B 6
      500 nℳ''; ''B 7 4 nℳ''; ''B 9 4 nℳ''; ''B 12 700 pM''; ''Myo-inositol 6 μℳ'';
      ''4-Aminobenzoic acid 60 nℳ''. Table uses the script-M molarity glyph; m-script-M
      is millimolar, not a mass unit. The main 2014 assay overrides phosphate, FeCl3
      and organic amendments; do not inherit the base phosphate or base Fe dose. Separate
      exact preparation passage (Media preparation): ''Media preparation Artificial
      seawater medium AMS1 ( Table 1 ) was derived from the artificial seawater medium
      AMP1 ( Moore et al. , 2007 ). Organic buffers (for example, HEPES and EDTA)
      were excluded to avoid potential toxic effects ( Zigler et al. , 1985 ) and
      the possibility that they might be used as substrates for growth ( Nörtemann,
      1992 ). After autoclaving, AMS1 was sparged with 0.1 μm-filtered CO 2 for 5
      h followed by sparging with air for 10 h to establish a bicarbonate-based buffer
      system ( Connon and Giovannoni, 2002 ). All vitamins and organics were added
      after autoclaving and sparging. The pH of the resulting AMS1 typically ranged
      from 7.5 to 7.7. ''. No parent amount or preparation step is changed or newly
      certified; this evidence is attached to the named study variant only.'

  description: AMS1 alternate-phosphorus utilization experiment in Carini et al. 2014
    Figures 1-2, reconciled against this imported formulation. Composite differences;
    no single relationship enum selected. Parent preserved.
  modifications:
  - 'Relative to this imported parent: pyruvate 100 micromolar (parent 1 millimolar);
    glycine 5 micromolar (parent 50 micromolar); methionine 5 micromolar (parent DL-methionine
    50 micromolar). The paper does not resolve methionine stereochemistry.'

    but its 117 nanomolar dose is overridden by the main assay.

    6 micromolar, 4-aminobenzoate 60 nanomolar. Parent contains only biotin 4 nanomolar

      concentration of 1.0 μM.''. Exact omission excerpt (Organism source): ''without

      grown on P i .''. These are separate contiguous excerpts, normalized for whitespace

      microarray protocol''s 1 millimolar pyruvate/50 micromolar glycine/50 micromolar
      methionine is not this alternate-P assay. Use the paper''s substrate identity;
      no additional protonation/salt-form equivalence is asserted.'

variants:
- name: Carini 2014 AMS1 2-aminoethylphosphonic acid utilization assay
  description: AMS1 alternate-phosphorus utilization experiment in Carini et al. 2014
    Figures 1-2, reconciled against this imported formulation. Composite differences;
    no single relationship enum selected. Parent preserved.
  modifications:
  - 'Relative to this imported parent: pyruvate 100 micromolar (parent 1 millimolar);
    glycine 5 micromolar (parent 50 micromolar); methionine 5 micromolar (parent DL-methionine
    50 micromolar). The paper does not resolve methionine stereochemistry.'
  - FeCl3 1 micromolar (parent 117 nanomolar). The AMS1 base source specifies FeCl3.6H2O,
    but its 117 nanomolar dose is overridden by the main assay.
  - 'Full vitamin mixture: B1 6 micromolar, B3 800 nanomolar, B5 425 nanomolar, B6
    500 nanomolar, B7 4 nanomolar, B9 4 nanomolar, B12 700 picomolar, myo-inositol
    6 micromolar, 4-aminobenzoate 60 nanomolar. Parent contains only biotin 4 nanomolar
    and thiamine 60 micromolar.'
  - AMS1 Table 1 base uses MgSO4.7H2O at 2.8 millimolar, not parent magnesium sulfate
    28 millimolar. Source hydrate forms also specify CaCl2.2H2O, MnCl2.4H2O, ZnSO4.7H2O,
    CoCl2.6H2O, Na2MoO4.2H2O and NiCl2.6H2O; corresponding parent forms are anhydrous
    or unspecified. Retain Table 1 molar doses for these unchanged-dose salts, without
    mass conversion.
  - 'No phosphate is added to the alternate-P assay base; omit the phosphate of original
    AMS1 Table 1. This is not a claim of zero residual phosphate: the Figure 2 inoculum
    was previously grown on phosphate.'
  - 'Added 2-aminoethylphosphonic acid: 1.0 micromolar final, numerically equal to
    the parent''s 0.001 millimolar. This supports the assay, not the complete parent
    recipe. Use the paper''s substrate identity; no additional protonation/salt-form
    equivalence is asserted.'
  - Base preparation follows Carini 2013 Media preparation (inorganic AMS1 autoclaved,
    then carbon-dioxide and air sparging; vitamins and organics added afterward),
    rather than the parent's generic dissolve-all/filter-all steps. Reported base
    pH 7.5-7.7 is not an optimum or a separate measurement of every 2014 assay.
  purpose: Test HTCC7211 utilization of 2-aminoethylphosphonic acid as an alternate
    phosphorus source.

  modifications:
  - 'Relative to this imported parent: pyruvate 100 micromolar (parent 1 millimolar);
    glycine 5 micromolar (parent 50 micromolar); methionine 5 micromolar (parent DL-methionine
    50 micromolar). The paper does not resolve methionine stereochemistry.'
  - FeCl3 1 micromolar (parent 117 nanomolar). The AMS1 base source specifies FeCl3.6H2O,
    but its 117 nanomolar dose is overridden by the main assay.
  - 'Full vitamin mixture: B1 6 micromolar, B3 800 nanomolar, B5 425 nanomolar, B6
    500 nanomolar, B7 4 nanomolar, B9 4 nanomolar, B12 700 picomolar, myo-inositol
    6 micromolar, 4-aminobenzoate 60 nanomolar. Parent contains only biotin 4 nanomolar
    and thiamine 60 micromolar.'
  - AMS1 Table 1 base uses MgSO4.7H2O at 2.8 millimolar, not parent magnesium sulfate
    28 millimolar. Source hydrate forms also specify CaCl2.2H2O, MnCl2.4H2O, ZnSO4.7H2O,
    CoCl2.6H2O, Na2MoO4.2H2O and NiCl2.6H2O; corresponding parent forms are anhydrous
    or unspecified. Retain Table 1 molar doses for these unchanged-dose salts, without
    mass conversion.
  - 'No phosphate is added to the alternate-P assay base; omit the phosphate of original
    AMS1 Table 1. This is not a claim of zero residual phosphate: the Figure 2 inoculum

  action: AUTOCLAVE
  description: "See separate recipes.  For approximately 1 litre of final medium,\

  action: MIX
  description: "Site selection for a good soil is very important and for most purposes\
    \ a soil from \r\nundisturbed deciduous woodland is best.  Sites to avoid are\
    \ those showing obvious \r\nsigns of man's activity and particular care should\
    \ be taken to avoid areas where \r\nfertilizers, crop sprays or other toxic chemicals\
    \ may have been used."
- step_number: 5
  action: STORE
  description: "A rich loam with good crumb structure should be sought.  Stones, roots\
    \ and larger \r\ninvertebrates should be removed during an initial sieving through\
    \ a 1 cm mesh.  The sieved soil should be spread to air dry and hand picked for\
    \ smaller \r\ninvertebrates and roots.  It should be turned periodically and picked\
    \ over again.  When dry it may be sieved through a finer mesh (2­4 mm) or stored\
    \ as it is prior to\r\nuse."

  action: AUTOCLAVE
  description: "Soil is prepared as above.  105 g of air­dried sieved soil and 660\
    \ ml of deionized \r\nwater are placed in a 1 litre bottle and autoclaved once\
    \ at 15 psi for 15 minutes, \r\nthen again after 24 hours.  The contents of the\
    \ bottle are left to settle (usually for \r\nat least a week) and then the supernatant\
    \ is decanted and filtered.  The final pH\r\nshould be 7.0 - 8.0."

    instead of 0.05 mM DL-methionine; the paper does not specify methionine stereochemistry.

    sulfate at 28.0 mM. Other unchanged Table 1 base-salt and macronutrient molar

    chloride hexahydrate as specified in Table 1; retain their Table 1 molar amounts
    rather than infer mass equivalents from the local anhydrous or unspecified forms.

    nM; Table 1 specifies the hexahydrate and its basal 117 nM is overridden by the
    assay methods.
  - 'Replace the imported biotin/HMP vitamin selection with the complete Table 1 vitamin
    mixture: B1 6 micromolar, B3 800 nM, B5 425 nM, B6 500 nM, B7 4 nM, B9 4 nM, B12
    700 pM, myo-inositol 6 micromolar and 4-aminobenzoic acid 60 nM. Do not substitute
    HMP for B1 using this 2013 paper.'

    the bicarbonate buffer by filtered CO2 then air sparging, and add vitamins and
    organics afterward; this differs from the imported all-ingredient filter-sterilization
    instruction. The reported resulting pH is 7.5-7.7, not an independently optimized
    value.'

- reference: doi:10.1186/1475-2859-8-29
  title: Genome, secretome and glucose transport highlight unique features of the
    protein production host Pichia pastoris.
  authors: Mattanovich D; Graf A; Stadlmann J; Dragosits M; Redl A; Maurer M; Kleinheinz
    M; Sauer M; Altmann F; Gasser B
  year: 2009
  notes: 'source_type=journal_article; discovery_mode=MediaDB_source_cross_reference;
    source 11, Medium 34; PMID:19490607; PMCID:PMC2702363; accessed_on=2026-10-13.
    Title, authors, year and DOI were verified against archived PubMed XML and publisher/PMC
    metadata; no PubMed correction/retraction notice was present. Inspected main article
    Strain and Experimental secretome analysis sections, and the complete additional-file-3
    workbook. Raw HTML/Markdown: references_cache/papers/primary_html/mattanovich-2009-pmc.{html,md};
    raw supplement and cell-addressed Markdown: references_cache/papers/supplements/mattanovich-2009-s3.{xls,md};
    abstract XML/Markdown: references_cache/papers/PMID_19490607.{xml,md}. The supplement
    distinguishes batch (A2:A11) from chemostat (A13:A22) formulations sharing trace
    stock (A24:A33). Batch cell A3 ends with an unlabeled ''1.8 g''; this dangling
    text is not assigned to an invented ingredient. The parent''s sulfate molarity
    cannot be certified from the sulfuric-acid volume/range without a verified density;
    chemical hydrates, acid/base forms and preparation also need separate parent review.
    The glucose chemostat formulation is represented in the named inline variant,
    not substituted for the parent. The bacterial category is a retained, known mismatch
    to this fungal strain, not an endorsed classification. Reported scientific name=Pichia
    pastoris; strain=DSMZ 70382 (=CBS704 in the paper). taxonomy_match=exact_strain;
    NCBITaxon:638632; canonical_label=Komagataella pastoris DSMZ 70382; rank=strain
    in NCBI Taxonomy XML retrieved 2026-10-13; source=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Browser/wwwtax.cgi?id=638632.
    NCBI lists Pichia pastoris DSMZ 70382 as a synonym; species ancestor=Komagataella
    pastoris, NCBITaxon:4922. Organism curation is limited to the source strain and
    chemostat passages. Other genomic comparator taxa, mutant-selection YP media and
    outside citations are not growth evidence for this record. KGX publication remains
    withheld because scoped_to_variant is not honored by the current exporter.'
variants:
- name: Mattanovich 2009 glucose chemostat formulation
  description: Source-defined glucose chemostat formulation, distinct from the imported
    glycerol batch medium. All recipe quantities retain supplement source units and
    stock/final boundaries; not a certification of the parent's concentrations, ingredient
    grounding or preparation.
  modifications:
  - Replace the batch parent's glycerol (433.27 mM) with glucose monohydrate at the
    source's 50.0 g per liter of chemostat medium.
  - Use 0.9 g/L citric acid, 1.7 g/L KCl and 4.35 g/L (NH4)2HPO4, replacing the parent's
    molar citrate, KCl and ammonium-phosphate entries; preserve the source's chemical
    forms and mass basis.
  - Use 0.01 g/L CaCl2 dihydrate and 0.65 g/L MgSO4 heptahydrate rather than inheriting
    the parent's batch amounts and anhydrous/unspecified forms.
  - Add 1 mL of 0.2 g/L biotin stock per liter of chemostat medium instead of inheriting
    the parent's direct biotin molarity.
  - Replace the parent's nine flattened trace/acid entries (sulfate, boric acid, sodium
    molybdate, manganese sulfate, ferrous sulfate, cobalt chloride, cupric sulfate,
    zinc chloride and sodium iodide) with 1.6 mL of trace-salts stock per liter of
    chemostat medium. Do not retain both the flattened ingredients and this stock
    dose.
  - 'Trace-salts stock, per liter of stock: 6.0 g CuSO4 pentahydrate, 0.08 g NaI,
    3.0 g MnSO4 monohydrate, 0.2 g Na2MoO4 dihydrate, 0.02 g H3BO3, 0.5 g CoCl2, 20.0
    g ZnCl2, 5.0 g FeSO4 heptahydrate and 5 mL H2SO4 (95-98% w/w). These are stock
    amounts, not final-medium amounts; no acid density or molar conversion is inferred.'
  - Set initial medium pH to 5.0 using 25% HCl as stated in the supplement; its percentage
    basis and a fixed titrant volume are not specified. The chemostat pH was controlled
    at 5.0 with 25% ammonium hydroxide. The inspected source does not establish the
    parent's generic final-medium filter-sterilization procedure, so that procedure
    is not inherited as verified study preparation.
  purpose: Glucose-limited chemostat cultivation for experimental secretome analysis.

    Markdown: references_cache/papers/primary_scans/jensen-1993/; raw abstract XML/Markdown:

    L. lactis strains and L. cremoris is inferred. Table 2 also reports NCDO 712 and

    controls. Exact caption excerpt, page 4364 Table 2: ''Growth of L. lactis subsp.
    lactis on solid medium containing six or more amino acids''; strain-column labels
    are ''712'', ''C2'' (2 printed as subscript), and ''MG1363''. Page 4363 identifies

variants:
- name: modified_dsmz_640_blumer_schuette_2010
  relationship: DERIVED_FROM
  description: Modified DSMZ medium 640 used for comparative Caldicellulosiruptor
    physiology (Blumer-Schuette et al. 2010).
  modifications:
  - Trypticase, cysteine-HCl, and resazurin omitted relative to standard DSMZ 640.
  - Carbon source increased to 5 g/L; Na2S.9H2O added to 0.5% final.
  - Anaerobic batch cultivation under N2; 70C with orbital shaking; 50 ml in 125 ml
    serum bottle; 24 h.
  purpose: Reusable variant for the 8 Caldicellulosiruptor DSM strains grown in modified
    DSMZ 640 in this study.
  evidence:
  - reference: doi:10.1128/AEM.01400-10
    supports: SUPPORT
    explanation: Blumer-Schuette et al. 2010 methods describe the modified DSMZ 640
      formulation and cultivation.
    snippet: subcultured ... into modified DSMZ medium 640 ... grown at 70C with orbital
      shaking under N2 headspace.
- name: modified_dsmz_640_shang_2013
  relationship: DERIVED_FROM
  description: Modified DSMZ medium 640 for Thermoanaerobacterium calidifontis Rx1
    (Shang et al. 2013); ferric iron, added SL-10/vitamins/resazurin, variable substrate.
  modifications:
  - 'Iron source substituted: FeCl3.6H2O 2.5 mg/L (vs ferrous iron in parent).'
  - Added trace element solution SL-10 (1 ml/L, DSMZ medium 320) and vitamin solution
    (5 ml/L, DSMZ medium 141, filter-sterilized).
  - Added resazurin 0.5 mg/L.
  - Fixed glucose replaced by variable substrate at 10.0 g/L (e.g. oat spelt xylan,
    xylose, glucose).
  - 'Per liter: 0.9 g NH4Cl, 0.9 g NaCl, 0.4 g MgCl2.6H2O, 0.75 g KH2PO4, 1.5 g K2HPO4,
    0.75 g cysteine-HCl.H2O, 2 g tryptone, 1 g yeast extract; pH 7.0; prepared under
    100% N2; dispensed 5 ml into 15 ml Hungate tubes; autoclaved.'
  purpose: Capture the explicit modified DSMZ 640 recipe used to isolate and characterize
    T. calidifontis Rx1.
  evidence:
  - reference: doi:10.1007/s00203-013-0895-5
    supports: SUPPORT
    explanation: Shang et al. 2013 prints the full modified DSMZ 640 recipe with explicit
      deviations from the parent.
    snippet: All culturing of Rx1 was performed in modified DSMZ medium 640, containing
      (per liter distilled water) 0.9 g NH4Cl, 0.9 g NaCl, 0.4 g MgCl2 x 6 H2O, 0.75
      g KH2PO4, 1.5 g K2HPO4, 2.5 mg FeCl3 x 6 H2O, 0.75 g cysteine-HCl x H2O, 2 g
      tryptone, 1 g yeast extract, 1 ml trace element solution SL-10, 0.5 mg resazurin,
      5 ml vitamin solution, 10.0 g substrate.

preparation_steps:
- step_number: 1
  action: AUTOCLAVE
  description: Dissolve ingredients (except sulfur, carbonate, vitamins, growth-stimulating
    factors and Na-dithionite), boil medium for 1 min, then cool to room temperature
    under 80% H2 and 20% CO2 gas atmosphere. Adjust pH to 6.0 and dispense under 80%
    H2 and 20% CO2 gas atmosphere into anoxic Hungate-type tubes or serum vials which
    contain already the appropriate amount of sulfur, only to 30% of their volume
    to allow for a large head space. Autoclave at a temperature of <b>110°C</b> for
    20 min! Add vitamins and growth-stimulating factors from sterile anoxic stock
    solutions prepared under 100% N2 gas and carbonate and Na-dithionite from sterile
    anoxic stock solution prepared under 80% N2 and 20% CO2 gas atmosphere. Vitamins
    and Na-dithionite are sterilized by filtration. Adjust pH of the complete medium
    to 6.0, if necessary.
- step_number: 2
  action: MIX
  description: After inoculation use 1 bar overpressure of sterile 80% H2 and 20%
    CO2 gas mixture.
applications:
- Microbial cultivation

    Additional exact excerpt: "Dissolve ingredients (except sulfur, carbonate, vitamins, growth-stimulating factors and Na-dithionite), boil medium for 1 min, then cool to room temperature under 80% H2 and 20% CO2 gas atmosphere. Adjust pH to 6.0 and dispense under 80% H2 and 20% CO2 gas atmosphere into anoxic Hungate-type tubes or serum vials which contain already the appropriate amount of sulfur, only to 30% of their volume to allow for a large head space. Autoclave at a temperature of <b>110\u00b0C</b> for 20 min! Add vitamins and growth-stimulating factors from sterile anoxic stock solutions prepared under 100% N2 gas and carbonate and Na-dithionite from sterile anoxic stock solution prepared under 80% N2 and 20% CO2 gas atmosphere. Vitamins and Na-dithionite are sterilized by filtration. Adjust pH of the complete medium to 6.0, if necessary."

preparation_steps:
- step_number: 1
  action: AUTOCLAVE
  description: Dissolve ingredients (except sulfur, carbonate, vitamins, growth-stimulating
    factors and Na-dithionite), boil medium for 1 min, then cool to room temperature
    under 80% H2 and 20% CO2 gas atmosphere. Adjust pH to 6.0 and dispense under 80%
    H2 and 20% CO2 gas atmosphere into anoxic Hungate-type tubes or serum vials which
    contain already the appropriate amount of sulfur, only to 30% of their volume
    to allow for a large head space. Autoclave at a temperature of <b>110°C</b> for
    20 min! Add vitamins and growth-stimulating factors from sterile anoxic stock
    solutions prepared under 100% N2 gas and carbonate and Na-dithionite from sterile
    anoxic stock solution prepared under 80% N2 and 20% CO2 gas atmosphere. Vitamins
    and Na-dithionite are sterilized by filtration. Adjust pH of the complete medium
    to 6.0, if necessary.
- step_number: 2
  action: MIX
  description: After inoculation use 1 bar overpressure of sterile 80% H2 and 20%
    CO2 gas mixture.
applications:
- Microbial cultivation

    Additional exact excerpt: "Dissolve ingredients (except sulfur, carbonate, vitamins, growth-stimulating factors and Na-dithionite), boil medium for 1 min, then cool to room temperature under 80% H2 and 20% CO2 gas atmosphere. Adjust pH to 6.0 and dispense under 80% H2 and 20% CO2 gas atmosphere into anoxic Hungate-type tubes or serum vials which contain already the appropriate amount of sulfur, only to 30% of their volume to allow for a large head space. Autoclave at a temperature of <b>110\u00b0C</b> for 20 min! Add vitamins and growth-stimulating factors from sterile anoxic stock solutions prepared under 100% N2 gas and carbonate and Na-dithionite from sterile anoxic stock solution prepared under 80% N2 and 20% CO2 gas atmosphere. Vitamins and Na-dithionite are sterilized by filtration. Adjust pH of the complete medium to 6.0, if necessary."
